author: GamingBolt
description:
Moss: The Forgotten Relic represents the virtual reality ecosystem losing one of its most unique and interesting exclusive experiences, which is a shame for those platforms but a welcome sight for the games. 

Both books of Moss tell a beautiful tale of a small but mighty mouse, an apt metaphor for a great game breaking out of its trappings on a less popular platform, and while its design loses some precision in the transition, the combination of the story, puzzles, and combat holds up as a lovable and emotionally impactful package, nonetheless. 

When the second book closes in-game, a third lights up nearby, and I hope moving Moss from its clearly intended home on VR to a broader audience on console allows us to see that third story.
title: Moss: The Forgotten Relic Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
We’re certainly stoked about the addition of cross-platform saves to Crimson Desert, believe us. But that doesn’t stop us from raising a few concerns about the way it'd been implemented, an approach that has left several gaps that the developer is going to have to fill besides having an entire roadmap of content planned out for the rest of the year. Can the studio manage to do that, or are we going to have to make peace with a system that’s undoubtedly functional, but in need of refinement?

As always, we’re happy to get into it and take you along for the ride. Strap in as we take a gander at why Crimson Desert’s latest update might be the first one to shave off a bit of the forward momentum it's been gathering up all year.
title: Crimson Desert Finally Has Cross Save, But Its Implementation Is Far From Seamless

author: GamingBolt
description:
When do you get to a point where the music starts slowing and it becomes even more obvious than ever that “Hey, maybe physical games don't have much of a future?" It was probably around the time Rockstar announced no disc when purchasing Grand Theft Auto 6 physically. Of course, we all know what happened next – PlayStation's announcement is probably the best case of the music outright stopping, even if it's still years off from happening. But lest we forget, many were (and remain) annoyed at Rockstar for the lack of a physical disc.

Which is a noble endeavor, don't get me wrong. But beyond how much more understated physical sales have become, the futility is underscored by the fact that GTA 6 is topping pre-orders on the PlayStation Store in pretty much every region. The United States, UK, Germany – the list goes on, and surprise, surprise, the Ultimate Edition is on top over the Standard Edition.
